mainTopic: The ברכה on water and the end of פרק כיצד מברכין; the משנה of זימון, its source, and whether two may make a זימון
overview: This amud closes the third chapter of ברכות and opens the fourth, פרק שלשה שאכלו. First the גמרא finishes explaining that someone who drinks water only to wash down stuck meat makes no ברכה. Then it asks whether the ברכה on water follows the תנא קמא (שהכל) or רבי טרפון (בורא נפשות רבות), and the answer is: go see what the people do. After the הדרן, the new משנה teaches that three who ate together must make a זימון. It lists who counts toward the three and who does not, and gives the minimum amount of eating: a כזית, or a כביצה for רבי יהודה. The גמרא finds the source for זימון in פסוקים where one person calls on others to praise ה׳. It adds that the one answering אמן, and the מתרגם, should not be louder than the main speaker. Finally רב and רבי יוחנן argue whether two people may make a voluntary זימון, and the גמרא pushes off challenges to the lenient view. The last answer, about a waiter, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Water drunk to free stuck meat needs no ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer about what the word 'לצמאו' comes to exclude: a person choking on meat who drinks water only to wash it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: (This excludes someone) who was choked by a piece of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the answer to a question begun on the previous daf. It explains that the משנה's word 'לצמאו' (for thirst) comes to exclude someone who drinks water only to dislodge food stuck in his throat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that one who drinks water 'for his thirst' says שהכל. The extra word 'for his thirst' teaches that the ברכה depends on enjoying the drink. A person drinking only to clear a stuck piece of meat gets no real pleasure from the water, so he says no ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: for his thirst (the word in the משנה being explained)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule behind many ברכות: a ברכת הנהנין is said only on food or drink that a person enjoys. Water drunk as medicine or to swallow something does not get a ברכה.

phrases.english: who was choked by a piece of meat.
phrases.notes: End of the sentence 'לאפוקי מאן דחנקתיה אומצא': this excludes one whom meat choked, who drinks water to wash it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, begun on the previous amud, to the question of what 'לצמאו' excludes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'לצמאו' excludes one who drinks water only to dislodge stuck meat. He makes no ברכה because he has no enjoyment.

steps.title: רבי טרפון's ברכה on water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second opinion: רבי טרפון says the ברכה on water is 'בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: (Over water one says) 'Who creates many living beings and their needs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי טרפון's opinion. This sets up the question that comes next: which opinion do we follow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said that water drunk for thirst gets שהכל נהיה בדברו. רבי טרפון disagrees and says its ברכה is 'בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן'. Quoting both views sets the stage for the גמרא to ask what the final הלכה is.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא who disagrees with the תנא קמא here

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי טרפון is talking about the ברכה BEFORE drinking water. Do not mix this up with the familiar after-ברכה בורא נפשות, which is said after drinking.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:
'Who creates many living beings and their needs.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the תנא קמא's wording to the second opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, the ברכה on water is בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן.

steps.title: Asking which opinion is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן asks אביי (or, some say, רב יוסף) what the הלכה is in this argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי (and some say, to רב יוסף): What is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן asks אביי (or רב יוסף) a direct practical question: in the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי טרפון, which opinion do we follow? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two opinions about the ברכה on water, and a person needs to know what to actually say. The גמרא records two versions of who was asked, אביי or רב יוסף, but the question is the same either way.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (a second version of the story)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye,
and some say, to Rav Yosef:
What is the halakha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a final ruling on the argument just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows the תנא קמא (שהכל) or רבי טרפון (בורא נפשות) for the ברכה on water.

steps.title: Go see what the people do
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב יוסף) answers: go out and see what the people are doing. Common practice decides the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go out and see what the people are doing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי (or רב יוסף) answers by pointing to common practice. The widespread custom of the people shows what the הלכה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of quoting a source, he relies on how ordinary Jews actually behave, which reflects an accepted tradition. People were saying שהכל before drinking water, so the הלכה follows the תנא קמא and not רבי טרפון.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה before water is שהכל, and the ברכה after it is בורא נפשות. When the הלכה is unclear, the established practice of the people can decide it ('פוק חזי מאי עמא דבר').
steps.whyThisMatters: 'פוק חזי מאי עמא דבר' became a well-known principle: accepted communal practice can serve as a guide for deciding הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Go out and see what the people are doing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the הלכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow common practice, which is to say שהכל before water. This is like the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing כיצד מברכין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the third chapter of ברכות, פרק כיצד מברכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'How do we bless?'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said at the end of a chapter. It marks that פרק כיצד מברכין is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a farewell to the chapter that expresses a hope to come back and learn it again. It separates the laws of the ברכות before and after eating from the next topic, זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How do we bless?', the name of the chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'How do we bless'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that the previous step finished.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter on which ברכות to say over foods is complete.

steps.title: Three who ate together must make a זימון
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with the basic rule: three people who ate together are obligated to make a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Three people who ate together are obligated to make a זימון (to join in inviting one another to say ברכת המזון).
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with its main rule. When three people eat a meal together, they must make a זימון before ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about each person's own ברכות. This משנה adds a group obligation: eating together creates a duty to say ברכת המזון together, with one person inviting the others. The key word is 'כאחת', meaning they ate as one group.

keyTerms.meaning: three who ate (also the name of the chapter)
to make a זימון, the invitation to bentch together

phrases.english: MISHNA: Three who ate as one,
are obligated to form a zimmun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter and a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people who eat together are obligated in זימון.

steps.title: Unusual eaters who still count for זימון
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists cases where a person still counts toward the three for זימון: one who ate דמאי, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, מעשר שני or הקדש that was redeemed, a waiter who ate a כזית, and a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one ate דמאי, or מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, or מעשר שני or הקדש that were redeemed; and a waiter who ate a כזית; and a כותי: we make a זימון with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes through a list of people who might seem not to count for זימון. It teaches that each of them does count toward the three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has a reason it might be excluded. Some ate food with a doubtful or special status (דמאי, tithes, הקדש), but because that food is permitted to eat, it counts as a real meal. The waiter was not sitting at the meal, but he ate a כזית from it, so he joins. The כותי's Jewish status is questionable, yet this משנה counts him.

keyTerms.meaning: produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed
first tithe, given to the לוי
second tithe and consecrated property that were redeemed, making them permitted
we include him in the זימון

steps.confusionAlert: 'מזמנין עליו' does not mean these people lead the זימון. It means they count toward the three needed to create the obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the guideline for the rest of the משנה: anyone who ate a halachically valid meal joins the זימון, even if the food or the person's status is unusual. The משנה will next list who does not count.

phrases.english: If one ate demai,
or first tithe whose teruma was taken,
phrases.notes: The תרומת מעשר was removed, so it is permitted to eat.

phrases.english: second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed,
and the waiter who ate an olive-bulk,
and the Samaritan: we form a zimmun with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines who counts toward the three just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eaters of permitted food of special status, a waiter who ate a כזית, and a כותי all count toward a זימון.

steps.title: People who ate forbidden food, a waiter who ate too little, and a non-Jew do not count
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists people who do NOT count toward the three for זימון: one who ate טבל, untithed or unredeemed holy foods, a waiter who ate less than a כזית, and a נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone ate טבל, or מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken, or מעשר שני or הקדש that was not redeemed, or a waiter ate less than a כזית, or a non-Jew ate with them, we do not make a זימון based on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite list from Step 7: people who cannot be counted toward the three needed for זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case here mirrors a case from Step 7, but with the food still forbidden (not tithed, not redeemed). Eating forbidden food is not a meal one can bless over, so it cannot join a זימון. The waiter who ate less than a כזית did not eat a real meal, and a נכרי is not obligated in ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which no tithes or תרומה have been taken yet; forbidden to eat
That were not redeemed (still holy, so forbidden to eat normally)
We do not count him toward a זימון

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this list up with Step 7. The cases look almost the same, but there the food was made permitted (tithed or redeemed), and here it was NOT. That one difference decides whether the person counts.

phrases.english: One who ate untithed produce,
and first tithe whose teruma was not taken,
and second tithe and consecrated food that were not redeemed,
and the waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk,
and the non-Jew — we do not make a zimmun on his account.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל טֶבֶל, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The negative mirror of the inclusion list in Step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who ate forbidden (untithed or unredeemed) food, a waiter who ate less than a כזית, and a נכרי cannot be counted toward זימון.

steps.title: Women, slaves, and minors are not counted with the men
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that women, slaves, and minors do not complete a זימון of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women, slaves, and minors — we do not make a זימון on their account.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another group of people who cannot be counted to reach the three needed for זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike Step 8, nothing is wrong with these people's food. The issue is their status: they are not counted together with the men to form the group of three. This rule is about joining the men's group. It does not say anything about whether they may make a זימון among themselves.

phrases.english: Women, slaves, and minors —
we do not make a zimmun on their account.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second category of exclusion, based on the person's status instead of the food
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women, slaves, and minors do not complete the three needed for זימון.

steps.title: How much must a person eat to be counted?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what the minimum amount of food is for someone to count toward זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to how much do we make a זימון? That is, what is the least amount a person must eat to be counted?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question to set up its next rule, about the minimum amount of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw that a waiter who ate less than a כזית does not count (Step 8). Now the משנה asks directly for the general minimum that applies to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to how much / what is the minimum

phrases.english: How much must one eat for us to make a zimmun?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the waiter's כזית detail into a general question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of food that makes a person count toward זימון

steps.title: An olive-bulk, or an egg-bulk according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a כזית is enough. רבי יהודה says one needs a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An olive-bulk is enough. רבי יהודה says: an egg-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question and records a disagreement about the minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion sets a low bar: a כזית counts as eating. רבי יהודה sets a higher bar: a כביצה, which is bigger. For him, a person must eat something closer to a real portion to be counted.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, the standard minimum amount for eating
The תנא who holds the higher amount

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is done: three people make זימון. Permitted food and status decide who counts. The minimum is a כזית (רבי יהודה: a כביצה).

phrases.english: — An olive-bulk.
Rabbi Yehuda says: An egg-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כְּזַיִת. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד כְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כזית according to the תנא קמא; a כביצה according to רבי יהודה

steps.title: What is the source for זימון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking which פסוק teaches the מצוה of זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things, that three who eat together must make a זימון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens on the משנה and asks for a source for זימון. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule but gave no source. The standard question מנא הני מילי asks for the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's basic rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the obligation of זימון

steps.title: רב אסי: 'Praise God with me'
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי learns זימון from the פסוק 'גדלו לה׳ אתי ונרוממה שמו יחדו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: Because the פסוק says, 'Praise ה׳ with me, and let us exalt His name together.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives the first answer to the source question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, one person speaks ('with me') and calls to others in the plural ('praise'). Plural means at least two others, so three people praise ה׳ together. That is exactly a זימון.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
As the verse states:
"Praise God with me,
and we will exalt His name together."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זימון comes from 'גדלו לה׳ אתי': one person invites the plural others to praise together.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: 'When I call the name of ה׳, give praise'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a different source: 'כי שם ה׳ אקרא הבו גדל לאלהינו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: We learn it from here: 'When I call out the name of ה׳, give (plural) greatness to our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו offers a second, alternative פסוק as the source for זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too one person speaks ('I call'), and the others answer in the plural ('give praise'). That is the pattern of זימון: one leads and the group responds. The two אמוראים agree on the law and differ only on which פסוק is the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Give greatness to our God (דברים לב:ג)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: From here:
"When I call the Name of the Lord,
give praise to our God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel answer to the same question, using a different פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זימון comes from 'כי שם ה׳ אקרא הבו גדל': the leader calls and the group responds.

steps.title: One who answers אמן should not be louder than the one blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר אבא uses רב אסי's פסוק to teach that the one answering אמן must not raise his voice above the מברך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר אבא said: From where do we know that one who answers אמן should not raise his voice more than the one making the ברכה? Because it says, 'Praise ה׳ with me, and let us exalt His name together.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the פסוק was just quoted, the גמרא brings a related teaching that comes from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יחדו, 'together', means the voices should be equal. The responder should not drown out the one leading. This is a new rule about how to answer, not about the source of זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: That he should not raise his voice

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule: when answering אמן, don't shout over the person making the ברכה.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan bar Abba said:
From where is it derived that one who answers amen

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יַגְבִּיהַּ קוֹלוֹ יוֹתֵר מִן הַמְבָרֵךְ —
phrases.english: should not raise his voice louder than the one reciting the blessing?
As it is stated: "Praise God with me,
and we will exalt His Name together."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַבָּא: מִנַּיִן לָעוֹנֶה אָמֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching, prompted by the פסוק quoted in Step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who answers אמן should not be louder than the מברך, learned from 'יחדו'.

steps.title: The translator should not be louder than the תורה reader
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן פזי teaches that the מתרגם may not be louder than the קורא. He learns it from the extra word 'בקול' in 'משה ידבר והאלהים יעננו בקול'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said: From where do we know that the translator may not raise his voice above the reader? Because it says, 'משה spoke, and God answered him with a voice.' The word 'with a voice' is not needed. So why does the פסוק say it? To teach: with משה's voice, meaning at the same volume.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second side teaching on the same theme: a second voice should not be louder than the first voice. This time it is about the public קריאת התורה and its Aramaic translation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בקול' looks extra, since answering is obviously done with a voice. An extra word must teach something. It teaches 'in משה's voice': the two voices were equal. So too the מתרגם must match the קורא and not overpower him.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who translated the קריאת התורה aloud into Aramaic
The one reading from the ספר תורה
There is no need for the verse to say (this word seems extra)
In משה's voice, at the same volume as משה

steps.whatToRemember: זימון comes from a פסוק of one inviting many (רב אסי or רבי אבהו). Two side rules follow: the one answering אמן, and the מתרגם, should not be louder than the main speaker.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said:
From where is it derived that the translator is not permitted
to raise his voice louder than the reader?
As it is stated: "Moses spoke,
and God responded in a voice."
For there is no need for the verse to say "in a voice,"
so why does the verse say "in a voice"?
In the voice of Moses (no louder than Moses' voice).
phrases.notes: The extra word teaches that the two voices were equal in volume.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין הַמְתַרְגֵּם רַשַּׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching on the same theme of not overpowering the main voice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מתרגם may not be louder than the קורא, learned from the extra word 'בקול' meaning 'in משה's voice'.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the rule about the translator's voice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that the מתרגם may not be louder than the קורא. It adds that if the מתרגם cannot speak as loudly as the קורא, the קורא should lower his voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: The translator may not raise his voice louder than the reader. And if the translator cannot raise his voice to match the reader, the reader should lower his voice and read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up what רבי שמעון בן פזי just said about the מתרגם and the קורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן פזי derived his rule from a פסוק. The ברייתא states the same rule outright, so it serves as support. It also adds something new: the voices should match, so if the מתרגם is weak, the קורא must come down to his level.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), introducing support
The translator who rendered the תורה reading into Aramaic for the listeners
The one reading from the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: The מתרגם may not be louder than the קורא. If he cannot be as loud, the קורא lowers his voice so the two match.

phrases.english: This was also taught (in a baraita):
The translator is not permitted
to raise his voice louder than the reader.
And if it is impossible for the translator
to raise his voice to match the reader,
the reader should lower his voice and read.
phrases.notes: So the two voices end up equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי שמעון בן פזי's rule from Step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון בן פזי's rule that the מתרגם may not be louder than the קורא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same rule explicitly

steps.title: Can two people make a זימון? רב and רבי יוחנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב and רבי יוחנן argue about two people who ate together and want to make a זימון. One allows it and one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Two who ate together. רב and רבי יוחנן disagree. One said: if they want to make a זימון, they may. The other said: even if they want to, they may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a מחלוקת about whether two people, who are not obligated in זימון, may choose to make one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that three people must make a זימון. The question here is only whether two may do it voluntarily. The גמרא does not tell us which of the two אמוראים holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an אמוראים teaching or argument)
One said (the speaker is not identified)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say which view belongs to רב and which to רבי יוחנן. Don't assume one or the other.

phrases.english: It was stated: Two who ate together,
Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — מְזַמְּנִין,
phrases.english: One said: If they want to make a zimmun, they may do so,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין.
phrases.english: and the other said: Even if they want to make a zimmun, they may not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of voice levels and opens a new question about זימון with two people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: one view lets two people make a זימון if they wish, and the other does not.

steps.title: The משנה says three, which seems to rule out two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lenient view from our משנה. The משנה says three must make a זימון, which implies two cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: Three who ate together are obligated to make a זימון. Three, yes; two, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה to attack the view that two people may make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is a דיוק, an inference from the exact wording. Since the משנה chose to say 'three,' it seems that fewer than three, meaning two, cannot make a זימון at all. That appears to refute whoever said two may do it.

keyTerms.meaning: They are obligated to make a זימון

phrases.english: We learned: Three who ate together
are obligated to make a zimmun.
Three, yes; two, no!
phrases.notes: An inference from the wording of the mishna.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת חַיָּיבִין לְזַמֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lenient view in Step 18 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that two people may make a זימון if they want to
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה specifies three, which implies two may not make a זימון.

steps.title: The משנה is about an obligation, and two would be voluntary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה only discusses an obligatory זימון. Two people making a voluntary one is a separate question.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is an obligation; here, it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the lenient view. It explains that the משנה's 'three' refers only to an obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word חייבין, 'obligated.' So the inference only shows that two are not obligated. It does not show that two are forbidden from choosing to make a זימון. That optional case is exactly what the אמוראים argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (in the מחלוקת of the אמוראים)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה requires three for an obligatory זימון. Whether two may make a voluntary זימון remains an open מחלוקת between רב and רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a rule stated for an obligation does not automatically forbid doing the same thing voluntarily.

phrases.english: There (in the mishna), it is an obligation;
here, it is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'three' seemed to forbid any זימון with two.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only says two are not obligated. A voluntary זימון with two is a separate case and stays under debate.

steps.title: Three who ate together may not split up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source saying three who ate together must make a זימון and may not split up. It infers that two cannot make a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Three people who ate together must make a זימון and are not allowed to split up. So with three, yes, there is a זימון. With two, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge the opinion that two may make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two could make a זימון, three people could safely split up. One person would bless alone, and the other two would still have their own זימון. The fact that three are forbidden to split shows that two cannot make one.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a source brought as a proof or a challenge.
To make a זימון, joining together for ברכת המזון
To split up, so each person blesses separately
Yes / no. This is how the גמרא draws an inference from a source.

steps.confusionAlert: The source never says outright that two cannot make a זימון. The גמרא reads that idea into it from the rule that three may not split up.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Three who ate together
are obligated to make a zimmun,
and are not permitted to split up.
Three: yes,
two: no!
phrases.notes: If two could make a zimmun, splitting up would cost nothing, since the remaining two would have their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new challenge to the lenient view, coming after the answer about the משנה in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that two people may make a זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three may not split up. That only makes sense if the leftover two could not make their own זימון.

steps.title: Three already became an obligated group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that three are different. They became an obligated group from the start, so they cannot trade it away for an optional זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because from the very beginning they set themselves up as a group with an obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by giving a different reason why three may not split up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against splitting comes from the obligation three people already have. It does not come from two being unable to make a זימון. Once there is an obligatory זימון, they may not drop it for a voluntary זימון of two.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. This formula shows that the case in the source does not compare to ours.

phrases.english: It is different there
because they established themselves with an obligation
from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּקָבְעוּ לְהוּ בְּחוֹבָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: an obligation already exists, unlike a voluntary זימון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three may not split up because two cannot make a זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three may not split up because they already have an obligation to make a זימון. Whether two may make a voluntary זימון is still an open question.

steps.title: The waiter serving two versus serving three
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a שמש serving two people may eat with them without permission. If he serves three, he needs permission. This suggests two cannot make a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A waiter serving two people may eat with them, even though they did not give him permission. If he was serving three, he may not eat with them unless they gave him permission!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source to challenge the view that two may make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two diners are assumed to welcome the שמש without asking, because he makes them three and lets them make a זימון. Three diners have no such need, so he must ask first. If two could already make a זימון, there would be no reason to treat two and three differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A waiter, the person serving the meal

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A waiter who was serving two people
may eat with them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתְנוּ לוֹ רְשׁוּת.
phrases.english: even though they did not give him permission.
phrases.notes: They are happy to have him, because he lets them reach three for a zimmun.

phrases.english: If he was serving three,
he may not eat with them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָתְנוּ לוֹ רְשׁוּת!
phrases.english: unless they gave him permission!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עַל הַשְּׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third challenge to the lenient view, after the second one (step 21) was answered in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that two people may make a זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שמש may join two without permission only because they need him for a זימון. That means two alone cannot make one.

steps.title: The answer to the waiter case begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins answering the challenge from the שמש with 'it is different there.' The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to push aside the proof from the שמש by showing his case is special. The full reason continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula 'שאני התם' tells us the גמרא will explain the שמש rule some other way, without relying on the idea that two cannot make a זימון. The reason itself has not been given yet.

phrases.english: It is different there
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the answer to the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (the answer is not finished on this amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שמש rule proves that two cannot make a זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שמש case has its own special reason, which is explained on the next amud.
